source_evidence: There is typically no transaction fee charged to the investor upon purchase, but the class of shares may pay 12b-1 fees.
answer: Retail no-load shares are mutual fund share classes commonly available to individual investors through a brokerage account, a fund family, or an investment advisory account. “No-load” does not mean there are no costs: these shares may have ongoing operating expenses, including 12b-1 fees, and a broker may charge transaction fees when you buy or sell some no-load shares. Compare the total fees and expenses for the particular share class, not just whether it has a sales load.
